What is the difference between RAM and storage?

RAM (Random Access Memory) is fast, temporary working memory that holds data currently in use by active programs, which is wiped when your computer restarts. Storage (such as an SSD or hard drive) is non-volatile, meaning it permanently preserves your files, documents, and programs even when powered off.
What is VRAM?
VRAM is Video RAM located directly on your GPU (graphics card). It stores graphics textures, framebuffers, and machine learning model weights during GPU computation, separate from system RAM.
What is a CPU?
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the primary processor of your computer. It executes instructions, performs logical and arithmetic operations, and manages system tasks.
What is a GPU?
A GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is a specialized processor built to perform thousands of mathematical operations in parallel. It excels at rendering graphics and training neural networks.
What is an SSD?
An SSD (Solid State Drive) is a storage device that stores data on high-speed flash memory chips without moving parts, making file reads and writes vastly faster than mechanical hard drives.
What is an operating system?
An operating system (such as Windows, Linux, or macOS) manages computer hardware, controls memory and disk access, and provides a platform for running applications.
What is a process?
A process is an active instance of a running program in memory. It has its own process identifier (PID), allocated RAM, and CPU execution time.
What is a memory leak?
A memory leak happens when a program allocates RAM but fails to release it after finishing its work. Over time, memory consumption steadily grows until the system slows down or crashes.
My app freezes when I open a large file. What should I check?
Check your system RAM usage to see if the file exceeds available memory. To fix it in code, stream or process the file in smaller chunks rather than loading the entire file into memory at once.
Should I close other applications first?
Yes, closing heavy background applications such as web browsers will free up available RAM and CPU resources for your active task.

Run `python -m venv .venv` in your project folder. On Windows, activate it with `.venv\Scripts\activate`. On Linux or macOS, run `source .venv/bin/activate`.
